title: Bougainvillea Vine Bracelet
category: Bracelet (a floral vine line bracelet: 5 prong-set cubic zirconia flowers set in line along a curving rhodium silver tone vine with pavé leaves and a fold over clasp; supplier Aditya, SKU ADT07, 3 colourways)
metal: Rhodium silver tone only. The tag is 'Rhodium Silver Tone Plated', and the description says 'Finish: Bright silver tone' and 'Plating: PVD rhodium coating, anti-tarnish'. The stems are mirror-polished. The leaves are pavé with a fine textured edge and a centre vein. Every metal part is rhodium silver tone: the vine, the prongs, the leaves, the joints and the clasp. There is no gold anywhere. The base metal is not stated. All 9 photos and Aditya's supplier photos show the same cool, bright tone.
lock: Rhodium silver tone, 17 cm. 1 slender S-curving vine with 5 prong-set flowers in line: 1 centre flower, about 11 mm, of 6 pear-cut soft lilac petals around 1 clear round stone, flanked by 2 round single-stone joints; 2 flowers each side, about 7 mm, of 5 pear-cut deep violet petals with 1 tiny clear centre. 6 stem curves carry 2 clear pavé leaves each (12). Fold-over clasp. The 5 flowers must stay small and graded (1 pale lilac 6-petal centre about a fingernail wide, 4 smaller deep violet 5-petal flowers), never enlarged, never all one size, colour or petal count.
morph: The flowers, in 4 ways. (1) Size. Every generation so far drew the centre flower about 1.3 times too big: about 15 mm on a 17 cm loop, covering about 30% of the wrist's width instead of about 22%. The small flowers came out about 1.2 times too big on the wrist. The owner flagged it, and all 7 listing photos of the time had to be warped down on 25 Oct (aditya-bracelets/build/retouch.py, README '25 Oct'). Check: the centre flower is about 1 fingernail wide and about 4.9 joint widths across, and each small flower is about 0.65 of it. (2) Count. The first Violet hero came out with 3 flowers and was rebuilt. Count 5: 1 centre and 2 on each side. (3) Grading. Models even the flowers out, giving all 5 the same size, the same number of petals or the same purple. The Violet colourway is two-tone by design: 1 pale lilac 6-petal centre and 4 deep royal violet 5-petal flowers. Models also push the violet toward fuchsia, magenta or ruby (Fuchsia is sold out) or toward pastel pink. (4) Structure. Models turn the inline vine into a chain or a tennis line with the flowers dangling as charms. They add extra buds, or paint the pavé leaves as green enamel leaves (a vine invites green). Second risk: the metal warms to 18k gold tone, since most of the catalogue is gold. Third risk: the fold over clasp becomes a lobster clasp, or the centre flower gains a halo or an extra ring of petals.
sizeMm: Listed: about 17 cm long. The description says 'Approximately 17cm'. Size guide photo 10 says '17 cm · fits wrists about 14.5–15.5 cm', which is a petite fit. Listed flowers: 4 small five-petal flowers, about 7 mm, and 1 six-petal centre flower, about 11 mm. My measurements are estimates. On Violet hero 04, the centre flower is about 160 px across, against a front loop about 850 px wide (about 54 mm if the 17 cm loop is round), so it measures about 10 to 11 mm and matches the listing. It spans about 4.9 of the round joints beside it (the README's 25 Oct measure), so each joint is about 2 to 2.5 mm. Each small flower is about 0.65 of the centre, about 7 mm. The pavé leaves are about 5 to 6 mm long. The fold over clasp plate is about 15 to 20 mm (foreshortened at the back of the loop). Body referent: in photo 07 (a size-corrected take), the centre flower covers about 22 to 23% of the wrist's width, about 1 fingernail. Each small flower is about the size of a little-finger nail. 3 flowers sit across the top of the wrist, the other 2 sit near the sides, and the clasp sits under the wrist (02).

claims: NONE. It has no Waterproof, Tarnish Free or Hypoallergenic tag (tags: Aditya, Bracelet, Cubic Zirconia, Demi Fine, Naira Petite, Rhodium Silver Tone Plated). The care text says 'Keep it dry and away from perfume and harsh chemicals', so it is not waterproof. Never show it in water, a shower, the sea or rain. The only finish facts the description supports are 'PVD rhodium coating, anti-tarnish' and the listing's own PVD-versus-plating line, quoted as material facts. They must not be upgraded to 'tarnish free', 'never fades', 'sweatproof', 'lifetime' or 'hypoallergenic'. It is not tagged pre-order.

story: A garden wall, shrunk to fit a wrist. The best fact about it is botanical. On a real bougainvillea the colour is not the flower: the papery magenta and violet 'petals' are bracts, and the true flower is the tiny white one in the middle. This piece does the same thing 5 times: coloured petals with a tiny clear stone at every heart. 'The colour was never the flower.' In India bougainvillea is the compound-wall flower. It spills over colony gates, old bungalows, Goa and Bengaluru villas and flyover planters. It is often called the paper flower (kaagaz ka phool), and in Bengali 'baganbilas', a garden's luxury. It blooms hardest in the dry, sunny months, and it is in full colour on north Indian walls through this winter. That is also the wedding season the listing names: a garden lunch, a sangeet. It thrives on neglect and dislikes being watered. So does this bracelet ('Keep it dry'), which gives an honest, funny line where a false waterproof claim would otherwise go: 'Likes it dry. Blooms anyway.' A history rhyme for an editorial frame: the plant is named after the French admiral Bougainville. As the story goes, it was collected in Rio in 1767 by the botanist Commerson and Jeanne Baret, who sailed disguised as a man and became the first woman known to sail around the world. Use it as 'as the story goes', never as a product fact. Visual rhymes: a mehendi bel (the henna vine that climbs the hand) running straight into the metal vine at the wrist bone; a herbarium sheet with the bracelet pressed under glassine beside a typed label; a seed packet whose back panel is the spec sheet ('Grows on wrists 14.5 to 15.5 cm'); a single-stem florist wrap in kraft paper ('Flowers that last past Monday'); crepe-paper flowers; a whitewashed gate where the fold over clasp hangs on the latch; a trellis; floriography (violet for faithfulness, lilac for first love). Colour strategy: Violet is the colour that has to sell. Its complement is marigold and saffron, and the listing's saffron-camisole worn shots already prove that pairing. Lime-washed or chartreuse grounds and deep peacock teal also make the lilac and royal violet sing. A wall of real magenta bougainvillea behind it competes and reads as the sold-out Fuchsia, so keep real blooms soft and out of focus, or use only their papery bracts and shadows. Crazy directions: (1) 'The colour was never the flower.': a macro beside 1 real bract and its tiny white true flower. (2) A herbarium plate: 'Bougainvillea, Naira Petite. Collected Nov 2026. 17 cm. ₹799.' (3) The vine as the end of a mehendi bel on the back of the hand. (4) A crepe-paper flower unfolds into the bracelet (motion: the paper moves, the jewellery never morphs). (5) 'Likes it dry. Blooms anyway.' on a sun-baked lime wall. (6) A seed-packet spec sheet. (7) 'Fuchsia sold out. Violet still in bloom.', only if stock is read again on the day of posting. Price line: ₹799, against ₹1,149.
copyNotes: Use: 'Bougainvillea Vine Bracelet'; 'a vine in bloom, around the wrist' (the listing's first line); 'five flowers'; 'a lilac centre flower'; 'deep violet'; 'pavé leaves'; 'a tiny clear stone at each heart'; 'cubic zirconia'; 'rhodium silver tone'; 'bright silver tone'; 'PVD rhodium coating'; 'fold over clasp'; '17 cm, fits wrists about 14.5 to 15.5 cm'; 'garden lunch'; 'sangeet'; '₹799' or 'Rs 799' (compare-at ₹1,149, about 30% off). Avoid: 'amethyst', 'tanzanite', 'sapphire' and 'diamond' (the stones are cubic zirconia; the Carré listings write 'not amethyst'). Avoid bare 'silver' (say 'rhodium silver tone') and any gold. Avoid 'sterling' and '925'. Avoid 'waterproof', 'tarnish free', 'sweatproof', 'hypoallergenic' and 'nickel free': it has none of those tags, and the care text says to keep it dry. Never upgrade 'anti-tarnish' to 'never tarnishes'. Avoid 'adjustable' and 'one size fits all' (it is a fixed 17 cm, a petite fit). Avoid 'charm bracelet', 'tennis bracelet', 'chain', 'bangle' and 'cuff' (it is a linked vine with the flowers set in line). Avoid 'six flowers', 'five-petal centre' and 'green leaves'. Never present fuchsia, ruby, pink or white as the colour shown (Fuchsia is sold out and White has 1 left). Never use the launch price ₹1,499 or ₹2,000. Avoid 'real flower', 'natural', 'botanically accurate' (a real bougainvillea has 3 bracts) and 'handmade' (not stated). If you quote the Jeanne Baret story, say 'as the story goes'. No brand comparisons.
